title: Beginner course
notation: One character per 16th note (4 per beat): 16 per bar in 4/4, 12 in 3/4 and 6/8, 20 in 5/4, 24 in 12/8. A lesson's (or unit's) "meter" sets the time signature, 4/4 if not given. x = hit, X = accent, g = ghost note (soft), . = rest. Separate bars with |. A lane's pattern repeats if it is shorter than the others.

units.title: 1. Keeping time
units.about: Steady quarter notes: the heartbeat of every groove. Count 1, 2, 3, 4 out loud as you play.

lessons.title: Quarter notes on the snare
lessons.tip: One hit per click. Let the stick bounce back up after each hit.

lessons.title: Quarter notes on the hi-hat
lessons.tip: Keep the hi-hat pedal pressed down with your left foot so the hi-hat stays closed.

lessons.title: Kick drum on every beat
lessons.tip: Play from the ankle, heel down, and let the beater come back off the head.

lessons.title: Hands and feet together
lessons.tip: Hi-hat and kick land at exactly the same moment. Listen for one sound, not two.

units.title: 2. Your first rock beat
units.about: Eighth notes on the hi-hat, snare on 2 and 4, kick on 1 and 3. The beat behind thousands of songs.

lessons.title: Eighth notes on the hi-hat
lessons.tip: Two even hits per click. Count "1 and 2 and 3 and 4 and".

lessons.title: Add the backbeat
lessons.tip: The snare lands on 2 and 4, together with the hi-hat.

lessons.title: The basic rock beat
lessons.tip: Kick on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, hi-hat on every eighth. Go slow until it feels automatic.

lessons.title: Rock beat at 90 BPM
lessons.tip: Same beat, a bit faster. Stay relaxed: tension makes you rush.

units.title: 3. Kick drum variations
units.about: Moving the kick around is the easiest way to make a beat your own.

lessons.title: Kick on the "and" of 3
lessons.tip: The extra kick sits between beat 3 and beat 4, with the hi-hat.

lessons.title: Kick on the "and" of 2
lessons.tip: This one pushes forward: the kick comes just after the snare on 2.

lessons.title: Two-bar kick pattern
lessons.tip: Bar one and bar two have different kick parts. Watch the bar numbers.

lessons.title: Four on the floor
lessons.tip: Kick on every beat, like dance and disco music.

units.title: 4. Sixteenth notes
units.about: Four notes per beat. Alternate your hands (right, left, right, left) on the hi-hat.

lessons.title: Sixteenths on the hi-hat
lessons.tip: Count "1 e and a, 2 e and a". Keep every note the same volume.

lessons.title: Sixteenth-note groove
lessons.tip: Right hand moves to the snare on 2 and 4 while the left keeps the hi-hat going.

lessons.title: Accents on the beat
lessons.tip: Play the first hi-hat note of each beat louder than the other three.

lessons.title: Syncopated kick
lessons.tip: The kick lands on the "a" before beat 3. Count the sixteenths.

units.title: 5. Ride and crash
units.about: Cymbals give a song its sections: the ride for big choruses, a crash to mark the start of a phrase.

lessons.title: Rock beat on the ride
lessons.tip: Same beat as before, but your right hand plays the ride cymbal instead of the hi-hat.

lessons.title: Crash on beat 1
lessons.tip: Hit the crash together with the kick at the start of each two-bar phrase, then back to the hi-hat.

lessons.title: Four-bar phrase
lessons.tip: Crash on bar 1, then three bars of groove. Feel the four bars as one phrase.

units.title: 6. Fills
units.about: A fill is a short break from the beat that leads into the next section. Keep the tempo steady through it.

lessons.title: Snare fill on beat 4
lessons.tip: Three beats of groove, then four sixteenths on the snare. Come back in with the kick on 1.

lessons.title: Down the toms
lessons.tip: Two hits each on the high, mid and floor tom, then crash back into the beat.

lessons.title: Groove, fill, crash
lessons.tip: Three bars of groove and a one-bar sixteenth fill around the kit. The crash on 1 tells everyone the fill is over.

units.title: 7. Rudiments
units.about: The building blocks of drumming, played on the snare. The app can't see which hand you use, so follow the sticking in each tip.

lessons.title: Single strokes (eighths)
lessons.tip: Alternate hands: R L R L. Both hands should sound exactly the same.

lessons.title: Single strokes (sixteenths)
lessons.tip: R L R L at sixteenths. Keep the sticks low and relaxed.

lessons.title: Double strokes
lessons.tip: R R L L. Two even strokes per hand: the second one is as loud as the first.

lessons.title: Paradiddle
lessons.tip: R L R R  L R L L. Accent the first note of each group.

units.title: 8. Ghost notes
units.about: Very soft snare notes between the backbeats. They make a groove feel alive. Watch the hollow notes: play them barely touching the snare.

lessons.title: First ghost notes
lessons.tip: Ghost notes from a couple of centimetres above the head; backbeats from high up.

lessons.title: Ghost-note groove
lessons.tip: Two ghost notes around each backbeat. Keep the hi-hat steady and the ghosts quiet.

lessons.title: Sixteenth-note ghost groove
lessons.tip: The hardest one: kick and ghost notes weave between the hi-hats. Start at a low speed.

units.title: 9. Open hi-hat
units.about: Lift your hi-hat foot so the cymbals ring, then press it down to close them again. Notes marked with a small circle are open. On an e-kit this needs a hi-hat pedal.

lessons.title: Open hi-hat on the "and" of 4
lessons.tip: Lift your left foot as you hit the open note, and press it down again on beat 1 so the hi-hat closes with the kick.

lessons.title: Two open hi-hats
lessons.tip: Open on the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 4; the foot closes the hi-hat on the backbeat and on beat 1.

lessons.title: Disco beat
lessons.tip: Foot down on every beat, open on every "and". The hi-hat should sound like "tss-chick".

units.title: 10. Beyond 4/4
units.about: Not every song counts to four. Count out loud with the click: "1 2 3" in 3/4, and in 6/8 and 12/8 the click comes every three eighth notes, so count "1 2 3 4 5 6" with the click on 1 and 4.

lessons.title: Waltz beat in 3/4
lessons.tip: Kick on 1, snare on 2 and 3: "boom chick chick". The click is louder on beat 1.

lessons.title: Rolling groove in 6/8
lessons.tip: Six even hi-hats a bar. The kick is on 1 and the snare on 4, right on the second click.

lessons.title: Slow blues in 12/8
lessons.tip: Four clicks a bar, three hi-hats to each click. Kick on clicks 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4, like a slow 4/4.

lessons.title: Groove in 5/4
lessons.tip: Five beats: think of it as 3 + 2. Kick on 1 and 4, snare on 3 and 5.
